## Lead notes (2026-11-27)
- Lithium mining 77% of USGS world 2025 (sites) — gaps: China (lepidolite mines' output undisclosed; task SC030), Zimbabwe
  (no per-mine output; SC030). Australia >100% because FY26 (Jul 2025–Jun 2026) figures and a 6% grade assumption for
  Greenbushes (D-104).
- Nickel mining: Indonesian output is captured at smelters (CGS dataset: 2.37 Mt Ni-equivalent operating capacity) because
  mines report wet ore; non-Indonesian mines/refineries still to research (SC021).
- Cobalt: CMOC (117.5 kt) discloses only a group total — counted as company-level; Indonesian MHP cobalt not split by plant.
- Graphite: China (1.4 Mt) mines not yet researched (SC016); ex-China mines ~45% covered.
- Processing (China): company-disclosed output of the companies whose 2025 annual reports we read covers 57% of China
  cathode output, 75% of anode shipments, 63% of separator, 59% of electrolyte, 43% of lithium chemicals. Site-level
  capacity is lower because most Chinese filings give company totals only (kept as unallocated company capacity, no location).
- SC030 (2026-11-27): China lithium mine coverage ≈67% of USGS after adding Jianxiawo (analyst-based estimate, 0.4),
  Lijiagou, Dangba, Qinghai 40 kt. Qinghai province reported 169 kt Li2CO3 in 2025 (government work report) vs 55 kt in our
  plant rows: the unattributed ~114 kt sits with CITIC Guoan, Dongtai, Yiliping, Huixin (no plant-level disclosure).
  Zimbabwe: no mine publishes full-year 2025 output; national exports 1.128 Mt concentrate (MMCZ) ≈ USGS 28 kt Li at ~5.3% Li2O.
